raw_text: [[File:{{{Alt}}}|28px|link=]] "From the cosmos, to your army ! This lob-loving duo will throw themselves at anything for up-close damage. When separated, Meteormites will attack nearby targets or find a friend to form a Meteor Golem!" Level 1 Level 2 Level 3 Contents 1 Summary 2 Strategies 2.1 Offensive Strategies 2.2 Defensive Strategies 3 Upgrade Differences 4 Statistics 4.1 As Temporary Troop 5 History 6 Audio 7 Gallery 8 Trivia 8.1 General 8.2 Comparisons Summary [ ] The Meteor Golem is the nineteeth Elixir Troop and currently the last one unlocked by upgrading the Barracks to level 19. Originally, the Meteor Golem was a Temporary Troop introduced in the Cosmic Rock event. They were unlocked after accumulating 100 Cosmic Shards in the event. The Meteor Golem comprises of two Meteormites stacked on top of each other. As a Meteor Golem, the method of attack is to have one Meteormite throw the other at their target, causing damage. This attack also splits the pair apart, but they can combine together again, either with each other, or with another Meteormite, to form a Meteor Golem and repeat the attack. Each Meteormite spawned through this attack starts with half the current health of the Meteor Golem, rounded down to the nearest 1% of Meteormite health. Thus a damaged Meteor Golem will spawn damaged Meteormites upon splitting up. Cloned Meteor Golems, when separated, cannot be merged back into the original unit. The same is true of Meteor Golems put into a defensive Clan Castle . Each time they recombine, they will become immune to damage for a short time. The total health of the Meteor Golem is determined by the health of both Meteormites, and will be subtracted if one or both of them take (s) damage. For example, if the Meteor Golem launches a Meteormite and takes another one from the other Meteor Golem, the total health of that merged unit may be higher or lower, even the level will either be lower or higher. As mentioned before, when they throw again, the hitpoints of the Meteor Golem will equally be split in half, even if the Meteormites were damaged previously before merging in the first place. Its Meteormites can jump over Walls without the use of Jump Spells , but Meteor Golems themselves cannot. Meteor Golems have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Meteor Golems will proceed to attack the nearest structure. Strategies [ ] Offensive Strategies [ ] Using Meteor Golems is considered to be one of the best attack strategies in the game, especially at Town Halls 17-18, in tandem with the Warden Charge ( Fireball and Rage Gem equipped). Once the funnel is set, the Meteor Golems will wreak havoc on to the base, provided if they are supported by units that target air, like the Archer Queen . However, since they are slow-moving, it may lead to a time fail if the attack is not fast enough, so use cleanup troops like Archers , Minions , and Wizards . An alternative to this strategy is to use the Royal Champion Charge to destroy defenses, but this is often risky because it may result in a time fail. Beware of high-damage defenses like single-target Inferno Towers , Monoliths , and Revenge Towers , as they can deal heavy damage to them. Use Freeze Spells or Overgrowth Spells to disable them, and Ice Block Spells or Totem Spells to tank the damage. Using the Overgrowth Spell can be risky however, because if the Revenge Tower was not on its full power and is trapped, it will eventually transform to its final state once the effect expires. Conversely, the Totem Spell can redirect the attacks and away from the army, in addition to defeating any Skeletons that would distract the Meteor Golems, which can be an advantage in attacking. The throw damage can be boosted by the Rage Spell, dealing more damage. If paired with Healers, the Meteor Golems themselves can also be regenerated significantly which also recovers both of the Meteormites' health, but when seperated, the Healers can heal the resulting Meteor Golem more effectively than when it is alone. Ice Golems can prove effective against Meteor Golems as they can freeze them for a short time, and results in a time fail. When they are deployed from the Clan Castle, use a Totem Spell to distract the Ice Golem from attacking them. Skeleton Spells can also work in this regard. Defensive Strategies [ ] Defending against Meteor Golems can be quite tricky, especially since their Meteormites can jump over Walls . Defending Heroes such as the Barbarian King can be very effective when countering Meteormites, as he has a lot of hitpoints, giving more time for defenses to defeat them, and can even disable their merging mechanics if they get to close, forcing them to attack him. Similarly, Ice Golems prove to be a valuable counter to Meteor Golems and their Meteormites, as they can also freeze them for a short time. Other units can also distract them for a short time, as they have a slow attack speed, like Skeletons from Skeleton Traps . Spell Towers , if placed correctly, can either do the following: When paired with defenses as the Rage Spell Tower, they can quickly ramp up damage to the Meteor Golems and Meteormites, eventually destroying them; If it is a Poison Spell Tower, it can help to slow down the advance of Meteor Golems, allowing more time for defenses to defeat them; or If it is an Invisibility Spell Tower, when a building is hit, it turns invisible along with the main defenses inside, forcing the Meteor Golems to retarget somewhere else that deals less damage while those inside can easily deal with them while defenses stay invisible. Make sure to place main defenses at the center, especially in ring bases, so that the Meteor Golems and its Meteormites will have a hard time going to the core. Upgrade Differences [ ] The Meteor Golem undergoes significant visual changes at all levels. Initially, the Meteor Golem appears to be two Meteormites stacked on one another. Each Meteormite is essentially a body/head of glowing blue eyes with cracks on its body/head. Each has thick, dark, aggressive, and expressive eyebrows, with arms attached to its body/head. The bottom Meteorite uses its arms to crawl and walk, while the top Meteorite has its arms raised. When it attacks, they split by throwing a Meteormite onto the nearest target, while the other will begin either walking towards another Meteormite to merge back into a Meteor Golem or to its target. At level 2, its body becomes orange and gains five yellow spikes on its head, with the center spike being larger. The eyes and cracks on its body are changed from blue to white. At level 3, its body turns blue, and the spikes on its head become white and start to glow. General [ ] You can have a maximum of 8 Meteor Golems at one time in a complete set of fully upgraded Army Camps . This number increases to 9 if you include 1 that can fit into a level 8 or higher Clan Castle . On the battlefield, you can clone an additional 4 Meteor Golems with four level 8 or higher Clone Spells (three from the regular spell inventory and one from a level 10 or higher Clan Castle). These total to a maximum of 13 Meteor Golems. The Meteor Golem is likely inspired by Geodude from Pokemon, except they are unable to levitate. According to the animation, The Cosmic Curse Awakens , Eternal Warden (Grand Warden's skin) is their creator as Eternal Warden learned a type of magic and fires a meteor and becoming a pair of meteormites. If a Meteor Golem performs their throwing attack while at less than 1% HP, only one Meteormite will spawn (where the throw lands), and it will spawn with 1 HP, and the one that throws it will just despawn, as it is presumably crumbled from using its ability. Comparisons [ ] Unlike other types of Golems, the Meteor Golem is an Elixir troop. The Meteor Golem is the first troop that can split into two subtroops and merge back into one. The Meteor Golem is one of the few Temporary Troops to later become a permanent part of the game. Unlike the others, it is the only one to return as a standard troop in the Home Village. However, in July 13-14, 2026, there was also an additional 60 temporary Meteor Golems added to the army only in Multiplayer and Revenge attacks, and the player can also use up to 8 of these permanent units as well. This created some interactions where two distinct Meteormite types do not fuse with each other (see Meteormite's trivia page ). The Meteor Golem has the most HP of any troop in the Home Village, even exceeding the Barbarian King at maximum level.
